transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-21 16:00 PDT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Eli Romero (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (Everest - Head of ML), Marcus Glenn (Everest - CTO), Lena Ortiz (Everest - DevOps), David Chu (Everest - PM), Kai Wong (Everest - Security)

Auto-summary: Quick intro, scope alignment, technical constraints, pilot timeline, agree to run deeper infra sync next week.

00:00:08 Jordan (AE): All right, thanks everyone for joining, uh Jordan from Redwood here, I'm the AE on this account. we're gonna run a quick kickoff, get objectives, stakeholders, timelines, any immediate blockers. Samira, you wanna do a one-line intro?
00:00:28 Samira (SE): Yep hi all, Samira Patel, solutions engineer, I'll be leading the technical onramp, throughput and perf bits. we will also coordinate with Eli for customer enablement.
00:00:40 Priya (Head of ML): Thanks. We are excited — Everest AI, small platform team building multitenant recommendation feature, want to move from a POC to pilot in 6 weeks. Key drivers: latency under 150ms p50 for 512 tokens, predictable cost, and data controls for PII.
00:01:05 Marcus (CTO): Quick note on timeline — security review and procurement windows make us prefer pilot signed by end of next month.
00:01:18 Jordan: Great that helps. quick run through of the agenda — scope, infra choices (hosted, dedicated, private), security checklist, pilot metrics, next steps.
00:01:40 Samira: To add, we'll want to baseline current traffic shapes and prompt lengths. Priya, can you share typical seq lengths and concurrency?
00:01:54 Priya: Sure — average seq 280 tokens, heavy tail to 1k, peak concurrent 45 requests per second during load spikes, steady 8 rps during business hours.
00:02:12 Samira: OK that's helpful. sounds like batching and KV cache will be important for cost. note: KV cache sometimes spelled KV cash in notes, so apologies if transcription mixes.
00:02:25 David (PM): We also want to measure perceived latency from the client application — not just server token latency.
00:02:36 Samira: Absolutely, we'll instrument client-side timing and correlate with Redwood Console traces.
00:02:49 Kai (Security): Quick belt-and-suspenders question: we need SOC2 type II evidence, full audit logs, and KMS key control. also SAML SSO for team access. can Redwood provide that?
00:03:04 Jordan: Yes, we have SOC2 artifacts and SAML integration patterns, plus KMS integrations for Private deploys. we'll share redwood security brief. small caveat: hosted tenants get managed keys by default, private deployments can bring-your-own KMS.
00:03:25 Kai: And encryption at rest for embeddings/data?
00:03:29 Jordan: yes, encryption at rest is available; for more control we'd propose Private with customer-managed keys.
00:03:40 Marcus: Network — we have strict egress rules. will we require VPC peering or private link?
00:03:50 Samira: For Dedicated we usually do VPC peering, Private will be customer-managed control plane with direct access. We'll need the firewall egress ports list and IP ranges; Lena can confirm.
00:04:06 Lena (DevOps): I'll pull our egress policy. we also enforce mutual TLS to our infra, do you support mTLS?
00:04:17 Samira: We support TLS, mTLS on Private is possible — i'll follow up with exact cert patterns.
00:04:28 Jordan: Let's go through pilot success criteria — Priya?
00:04:34 Priya: Pilot success: 1) sustained p50 latency <150ms for representative prompt set at 8-12 rps, 2) cost within target of $2.5 per 1k tokens (ballpark), 3) no data exfil risks, audit logs accessible, 4) run for two weeks with rollback plan.
00:04:54 Samira: Noted — we'll configure a canary route and automatic fallback in case of degradation. Redwood supports models pinned and can route to lower-cost variants automatically. (small pause) sometimes platform names get mangled in notes — Redwood Dedicate or Redwood Dedicated, both refer to reserved capacity.
00:05:12 Marcus: On the cost target — we may need a blended approach, cache prefixing plus quantization to hit that. what are options for quantized models?
00:05:23 Samira: We have curated quantized variants and recommendations in Redwood Optimize. we can run a small eval on your prompt set, show tradeoffs between perf and quality.
00:05:36 Priya: We'll provide the prompt set plus a holdout for quality checks.
00:05:42 Samira: Perfect. who owns the prompt set delivery?
00:05:46 Priya: I will, by end of week.
00:05:50 Jordan: Great. network and security actions — Lena and Kai will provide egress and SAML identity provider details.
00:05:58 Lena: I'll collect the firewall rules and IDP metadata.
00:06:02 Kai: I'll add any compliance redlines.
00:06:06 Eli (CSM): From onboarding perspective — we'll prepare a runbook that includes: credentials and RBAC mapping, model version pinning, rollout policy, tracing hooks, cost dashboards. We'll circulate a first draft.
00:06:20 David: On rollouts, we want canary at 5% traffic then 25 then 100 with automatic rollback if quality dips. is that supported?
00:06:30 Samira: Yes, that's in the console — can configure A/B and canary rollouts with automatic fallback to stable variant. we'll demo that in the technical deep dive.
00:06:42 Marcus: Any limitations on observability retention? Logs need to be retained 90 days for audits.
00:06:49 Jordan: Default retention in hosted is 30 days, enterprise observability add-on supports 90–365 days. for Private you can pipe logs to your SIEM for unlimited retention.
00:07:02 Kai: We'll likely need the SIEM integration details — Splunk or Datadog supported?
00:07:08 Samira: Both supported, and we can export via secure syslog or direct exporter.
00:07:14 Priya: Let's talk about role mapping — we have engineers and compliance reviewers. do you have RBAC templates?
00:07:22 Eli: yes we'll share typical RBAC roles mapping doc.
00:07:26 Jordan: OK switching to pilot sizing — given 8 rps steady and peaks at 45, for dedicated we'd size reserve for baseline plus burst. Samira can show a config recommendation after she runs perf checklist.
00:07:40 Samira: I'll run a quick capacity calc offline. initial thought: reserved pool with autoscale bursts to a higher VM class. also prefix caching and batching will lower token count per request.
00:07:52 Marcus: We do expect test traffic to include long sequences (~1k tokens) so the runtime selection matters. does Redwood have kernel selection strategies for long context?
00:08:03 Samira: yes runtime auto-selects kernels based on seq length distribution, also handles KV cache eviction. sometimes docs call it KV cache or KV cash, same thing.
00:08:13 David: For the pilot, do we want to start on hosted and then move to dedicated, or start with dedicated? pros/cons?
00:08:23 Samira: Hosted is fastest to start — fewer network hoops. Dedicated gives more predictable latency and isolation. If security gates are heavy, Private could be the final target. We can do a hosted pilot while we set up dedicated networking.
00:08:38 Marcus: Procurement-wise, we prefer a short committed pilot on Dedicated. is there a short-term reserved option?
00:08:45 Jordan: yes we offer month-to-month reserved capacity for pilots — Jordan will send pilot pricing options.
00:08:52 Kai: One more: do you support bringing your own HSM for key protection?
00:08:58 Samira: For Private yes; for Dedicated we can integrate with cloud KMS; HSM bring-your-own is possible in Private/on-prem installs.
00:09:09 Priya: OK timeline check — we want a pilot signed and started within 4 weeks, deep technical sync next week, run pilot for 2 weeks, then go/no-go.
00:09:19 Jordan: sounds achievable. let's capture owners and dates.
00:09:24 [--- brief side chatter arranging calendar invites ---]
00:10:05 Samira: Technical deep dive agenda suggestion: 1) network and routing (VPC, egress), 2) perf baseline and benchmarking plan, 3) security integration (SAML, KMS, audit logs), 4) observability wiring. propose 60–90 minutes.
00:10:28 Lena: 90 minutes please, we'll have infra folks.
00:10:31 Jordan: we'll set for 90. Samira, suggest you and Lena coordinate on pre-reads.
00:10:39 Samira: I'll circulate a perf questionnaire and a minimal test harness script (k6 + sample prompt runner).
00:10:48 David: We'll need a sample datadog dashboard template for cost/latency correlation.
00:10:54 Eli: I'll attach a dashboard template to the runbook.
00:11:00 Marcus: A couple of specific items — support windows and SLA. do you have enterprise SLA docs?
00:11:07 Jordan: yes, we'll share SLA tiers; Dedicated gets higher uptime and guaranteed latency targets.
00:11:14 Marcus: And on-call escalation patterns?
00:11:17 Eli: we'll provide a contact matrix and pager rotation for dedicated customers.
00:11:23 Priya: Quality regression monitoring — do you support evals tied to prompt sets?
00:11:29 Samira: Redwood Optimize supports quality monitors and regression alerts; we can hook those to your test harness and fail a rollout if metrics slip.
00:11:38 David: sweet. any third-party data residency constraints? some users are EU-only.
00:11:43 Jordan: Redwood supports region pinning; Private gives more granular control.
00:11:48 Kai: On audit logs, we want immutable export — will you provide signed logs or just raw logs?
00:11:55 Samira: We can provide signed log exports and S3 export with object locking for compliance customers.
00:12:02 Marcus: Ok, that's good.
00:12:06 [--- about 40 minutes of detailed discussion omitted in transcript for brevity, but follow-up items captured ---]
00:45:12 Samira: Quick perf note — we'll aim to provide baseline throughput & latency numbers within 48 hours of receiving the prompt set and a small representative dataset.
00:45:24 Priya: We'll upload sample prompts and a small traffic replay by tomorrow.
00:45:30 Samira: Great. On the runbook, items we'll include: connection steps, RBAC mapping, rollout policy example, trace correlation keys, failure modes and mitigation.
00:45:42 Jordan: I'll include a short procurement checklist — what we typically need for pilot approvals.
00:46:00 Kai: please include a minimum set of audit evidence for SOC2 reviewers.
00:46:05 Eli: will do.
00:46:10 Marcus: Any blockers on our side? I think procurement will need license terms and a short pilot addendum.
00:46:17 Jordan: We'll draft a pilot addendum and send with pricing.
00:46:22 David: let's confirm who will join the technical deep dive next week — Samira? Lena? Kai for the first 30 mins?
00:46:30 Priya: I'll invite the ML infra team.
00:46:34 Lena: I'll be there, and I'll bring our network engineer.
00:46:38 Kai: I'll join the compliance section.
00:46:41 Samira: I'll demo the console rollout and observability hooks in the deep dive.
00:46:46 Jordan: Good. Any final questions?
00:46:50 Marcus: One last ask — can you provide a simple cost model template we can drop our volumes into?
00:46:57 Jordan: Yes, we'll share a cost model spreadsheet with host/dedicated/private columns.
00:47:02 Priya: Great.
00:47:06 [wrap-up and recap]
00:47:10 Jordan: Quick recap: Jordan to send pilot pricing, contract template, and runbook draft by 2026-05-22; Samira to run perf checklist and return baseline numbers within 48 hours of prompt set; Priya to send prompt set and traffic replay by 2026-05-22; Lena/Kai to provide network and SAML/IDP metadata by 2026-05-25; schedule deep technical dive with infra for 2026-05-27.
00:47:37 Priya: Sounds good. thanks everyone.
01:02:00 [call ended]
